name: PLAID: An Efficient Engine for Late Interaction Retrieval
problem: Late interaction's query-time MaxSim scan over full-resolution document vectors was too slow for interactive search at scale.
mechanism: Treats every passage as a lightweight BAG OF CENTROIDS (cluster centroids over its token vectors) rather than its full token vectors, and prunes the centroid bags. Centroid interaction plus centroid pruning inside a highly optimised engine eliminates low-scoring passages early, so the full-resolution MaxSim only runs on survivors.
speedup_reported: Reduces late-interaction search latency by up to 7x on a GPU and 45x on a CPU versus vanilla ColBERTv2, while preserving state-of-the-art retrieval quality. Baseline (vanilla ColBERTv2) and hardware class (GPU and CPU separately) are both stated - this is one of the few retrieval papers with a CPU number, which matters because CPU-only retrieval serving is common. At 140M passages it reports tens of ms on GPU.
notes: VENUE: Semantic Scholar records CIKM 2022 ('International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management'); crossref did not surface a proceedings entry, so 'other' is used rather than guessing at 'kdd'. THE MOST IMPORTANT IDEA IN THIS SLICE FOR A SERVING ENGINEER: late interaction is a PRUNING problem, not a compute problem. Approximate candidate scoring first, exact MaxSim on survivors - the same coarse-to-fine pattern as speculative decoding, and the reason a 45x CPU speedup is possible when the tail of the score distribution carries most of the answer. It also shows why quantized or centroid-compressed indexes are a practical requirement rather than a nice-to-have at 140M passages.
